programme: RFX5 and RFXANK are obligate partners in the RFX transcription-factor complex (with CIITA, not in this list) that switches on the MHC class II locus — HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM/DO, exactly the near-identical target sets both factors carry here. NKX2-3 drives MADCAM1, the mucosal addressin that pulls lymphocytes into tissue, and PAX5 is the master commitment factor for B-cell identity. Together these three axes are the parts list for organizing a local antigen-presenting, lymphocyte-recruiting, B-cell-containing niche — i.e. tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation / ectopic lymphoid neogenesis, not a generic 'immune response'.
role_in_a: Nothing in the record ties this module to fibromyalgia specifically — Open Targets has no association for any of the four factors and no retrieved paper mentions fibromyalgia. If this axis is genuinely active in the blood-derived network, the more defensible reading is that it tracks circulating adaptive-immune cell composition (B-cell fraction via PAX5, MHC-II+ antigen-presenting cells via RFX5-RFXANK, gut-homing lymphocyte fraction via NKX2-3-MADCAM1) rather than a documented fibromyalgia mechanism.
role_in_b: Directly documented in gastric cancer: RFX5 promotes gastric adenocarcinoma growth, motility and apoptosis resistance and tracks with immune infiltration (PMID 41079601, 36045400); PAX5 marks lymph-node-metastasis-associated microenvironment changes and its methylation is used diagnostically (PMID 41992249, 39097885). These sit alongside the separately reported finding that FOXP3+ Treg content within tumor tertiary lymphoid structures affects gastric cancer prognosis (PMID 41892859) — consistent with the same TLS-building toolkit being active, though FOXP3 itself is excluded here as a carrier because it is flagged discordant rather than concordant.
shared_axis: Both networks light up the same lineage-defining, antigen-presentation/lymphoid-organization toolkit, but nothing retrieved connects chronic widespread pain to gastric tumor-associated lymphoid neogenesis. The more parsimonious explanation is convergence: any tissue sample with variable adaptive-immune cell content (tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in stomach, circulating lymphocyte subsets in blood) will show these same lineage TFs moving together, without that implying a shared disease mechanism.
reasoning: The programme is real and nameable — RFX5/RFXANK are a documented obligate complex with essentially identical target sets, and RFX5 and PAX5 are each independently and specifically placed in gastric cancer by two papers apiece. But NKX2-3's one paper is only tentatively about it (autophagy signature study, factor involvement unconfirmed from the snippet), RFXANK's sole paper does not mention gastric cancer at all, and every factor shows zero Open Targets association and zero papers for fibromyalgia. So the module is credible on the cancer side but the cross-disease link rests entirely on cell-composition reasoning, not on anything retrieved — textbook 'unexpected' with moderate rather than strong grounding.
support: PMID 41079601 — RFX5 drives gastric adenocarcinoma proliferation, motility, apoptosis resistance; PMID 36045400 — RFX5 as prognostic/immune-infiltration biomarker in stomach adenocarcinoma; PMID 41992249 — PAX5 role and regulatory mechanism in gastric cancer single-cell/spatial data; PMID 39097885 — PAX5 methylation as a gastrointestinal cancer diagnostic marker; PMID 41892859 — FOXP3+ tertiary lymphoid structure cells affect gastric cancer prognosis (context for the TLS story, not a carrying-factor citation since FOXP3 is discordant here); PMID 38617515 — autophagy-related gastric cancer signature study that likely but not confirmedly involves NKX2-3. No PMID above mentions fibromyalgia.
how_to_falsify: Deconvolve the fibromyalgia blood samples for cell-type fractions (e.g. CIBERSORTx or flow data) and regress RFX5/RFXANK/PAX5/NKX2-3 network activity against B-cell and monocyte/DC proportions: if the apparent 'module' tracks cell fraction rather than within-cell-type regulatory rewiring, the shared-axis claim collapses to a composition artifact. Separately, check whether RFX5/PAX5 target occupancy (e.g. ChIP or ATAC) in fibromyalgia PBMCs actually overlaps the same sites bound in gastric tumor tissue (RFX5 is ReMap-observed at 9/17 targets here) — no overlap would argue against a shared mechanistic axis even if both diseases show the factors as 'active'.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (fibromyalgia) versus stomach tumor tissue (cancer) — fundamentally different compartments, so any agreement plausibly reflects shared use of lineage-defining TFs by immune cells wherever they sit, not tissue-matched biology. The 120 patient-group comparisons come from a single independent cohort pair, so this is one cohort split many ways, not independent replication — treat the supported_in fractions (66–91/120) as far less robust than a same-sized count drawn from many cohorts. FOXP3 has the highest recurrence (91/120) of any factor here but is discordant, not concordant — it is the strongest single signal in the data and was deliberately excluded from the account for that reason. The single-view list (RFX1, TCF7, NKX6-3, TAF1, PRDM10, TBPL1, HOXD8, KAT5, PAX2, NR2C2, NPM1, CNOT7) shows the field is noisy enough that many TFs top one subgroup and vanish, which is why only recurrent, mechanistically linked factors were used to carry the story. Classic immune master regulators (CIITA, KLF2, SPIB, STAT5B, BCL3, PBX1, FOXO1, EZH2, HLX, KLF9, BRCA1, SMAD3) were already removed as tissue-generic, so RFX5/RFXANK/PAX5/NKX2-3 are not simply 'this is immune tissue' — but they remain lineage/composition-sensitive factors and should be read with that caution.
